Rates are crude (not risk-adjusted; case mix differs between groups, so a higher rate is no judgement of quality); readmission is all-cause within thirty days of an inpatient discharge, planned readmissions not removed; money by payer or plan follows member volume (no member months here). This file has exact dates: a limited data set, not de-identified. Service months from Aug 2026 on are incomplete: claims keep arriving for about 3 months after the service, so a drop there is lag, not a trend.

executive_view.headline: This healthcare claims dataset covers 2,668 claims across 403 members over 12 months, with $257,150.19 paid against $293,787.43 allowed and a 9.5% claim denial rate.

paragraphs.text: The dataset spans 12 months of service activity, with Northwind Health accounting for the largest share of paid spend and month-over-month paid amounts showing notable swings.
Outliers are present in paid and allowed amounts, and service months from August 2026 onward are incomplete due to claims lag, so recent figures should be read with caution.

findings.text: Northwind Health is the highest-spend payer at $113,095.83 paid, well above Summit Mutual ($49,026.14), Lakeside Care ($38,167.93), Harbor Senior Plans ($34,968.60), and Crescent Health ($21,891.69).

Paid amounts are skewed: the median paid amount per claim line is $33.52 while the mean is $57.68, with values ranging from $0 to $506.26, indicating a small number of high-cost claims pulling the average up.

Month-over-month paid amounts are volatile — paid amount rose 6.3% in Jul 2026 versus Jun 2026 — though with only 11 full months and no prior-year comparison, it is not possible to separate trend from seasonality.
The overall claim denial rate stands at 9.5%, and 230 voided claim rows were excluded from all money and denial calculations.

Read as P&C insurance data (incurred losses, paid losses, open case reserves, claims, severity (incurred per claim), policies). Losses are reported (case-incurred: paid to date plus case reserves) as of the latest valuation, with no IBNR and no loss-adjustment expense, in nominal dollars with no trend applied; loss ratios use earned premium. Lines differ in mix and exposure units, so a total across lines is a mix of them.
Sep 2026 is partial (data through the 28th) and is left out of period comparisons.
34,280 earlier valuations of claims are left out: only each claim and claimant's latest valuation counts.

As of the 30 Sep 2026 valuation, 2026 (9 months) and 2025 (21 months) are still developing: their losses will usually rise as claims are reported and reserves change, so they are not final and not comparable with mature years (liability lines develop beyond 24 months).
